rules.title: Define value before volume
rules.if: the program has no defined qualified business event
rules.then: define the event, qualification rule, owner, and estimated contribution value before optimizing traffic
rules.else: use the existing qualified event as the primary business outcome
rules.guardrails: Do not substitute sessions or ranking counts for value.

rules.title: Traffic is diagnostic, not the north star
rules.if: organic traffic increases AND qualified conversions or margin do not
rules.then: diagnose intent quality, audience fit, next-action continuity, and attribution
rules.else: continue scaling only while downstream value and guardrails remain healthy
rules.guardrails: lead quality, sales capacity, refund rate

rules.title: Separate forecasts from actuals
rules.if: search volume, CTR, conversion, or revenue is estimated
rules.then: label the output as a forecast and record every assumption
rules.else: use observed query, conversion, revenue, and margin data

rules.title: Respect fulfillment capacity
rules.if: expected qualified demand exceeds delivery or sales capacity
rules.then: prioritize higher-margin, higher-fit clusters OR increase capacity before expanding volume

rules.title: Model offers separately
rules.if: different offers have materially different audiences, margins, sales cycles, or qualification rules
rules.then: assign separate value models and cluster portfolios
rules.else: a shared model may be used with explicit segment dimensions

rules.title: Count assisted value carefully
rules.if: an informational asset rarely receives last-click conversions but appears in qualified journeys
rules.then: measure assisted progression, returning users, branded demand, and controlled lift
rules.else: judge the asset on direct value and task completion

rules.title: Split branded and non-branded demand
rules.if: brand familiarity materially changes intent, CTR, or conversion
rules.then: report branded and non-branded performance separately

rules.title: Include retention and expansion
rules.if: organic search serves existing customers, support, renewal, or repeat purchase tasks
rules.then: assign retention events and lifetime-value effects
rules.else: use acquisition outcomes for new-user clusters

rules.title: Raise evidence thresholds for high stakes
rules.if: the topic can materially affect health, money, safety, legal rights, or major decisions
rules.then: require qualified review, primary sources, explicit limitations, and stronger maintenance

rules.title: Resolve competing goals explicitly
rules.if: traffic, lead quality, margin, brand, retention, and learning objectives conflict
rules.then: name one primary objective and classify the others as constraints or secondary outcomes

rules.title: Allocate by marginal value
rules.if: multiple valid initiatives compete for limited resources
rules.then: rank them by expected incremental value divided by effort, risk, maintenance, and time to learning

rules.title: Use economic stop rules
rules.if: expected remaining incremental value is below expected cost OR risk exceeds tolerance
rules.then: stop, defer, retire, or redesign the initiative
rules.else: continue to the next defined review point

rules.title: Require an audience-task pair
rules.if: a candidate query cannot be mapped to a plausible audience and task
rules.then: classify it as uncertain and gather evidence
rules.else: attach the audience, condition, task, and journey state

rules.title: Treat funnel modifiers as heuristics
rules.if: a word such as how, best, review, price, or buy suggests a journey stage
rules.then: use it as a hypothesis and verify the actual task and result set
rules.else: infer stage from the full query, context, and behavior

rules.title: Model the funnel as a graph
rules.if: journey analysis assumes every user enters at awareness and moves linearly
rules.then: allow entry, exit, return, skip, and backward transitions

rules.title: Use adjacent next actions
rules.if: the proposed CTA requires substantially more trust or commitment than the current task supports
rules.then: offer an adjacent useful action OR add the proof needed to justify the transition

rules.title: Split materially different audience needs
rules.if: two audience segments require different evidence, terminology, constraints, or offers
rules.then: create distinct sections, experiences, or canonical assets based on task compatibility

rules.title: Include accessibility conditions
rules.if: the task depends on visual, motor, auditory, cognitive, or assistive-technology access
rules.then: design the format, navigation, media, and controls for those conditions
rules.else: apply baseline accessible design to all assets

rules.title: Require real local distinctness
rules.if: a geography modifier is proposed as a separate page
rules.then: require actual service eligibility, local evidence, local differences, and maintainable data
rules.else: consolidate into a broader service-area asset

rules.title: Localize, do not merely translate
rules.if: language or country versions differ in terminology, regulation, inventory, currency, or user expectations
rules.then: localize content and targeting signals
rules.else: use a shared translation only where the task and facts truly remain equivalent

rules.title: Account for device context
rules.if: device changes task conditions or interface needs
rules.then: adapt layout, media, interaction, and next action while preserving canonical meaning

rules.title: Match evidence to urgency
rules.if: the user has high urgency or high perceived risk
rules.then: front-load direct answers, scope, availability, proof, and safe next actions

rules.title: Explicitly exclude wrong audiences
rules.if: queries attract jobs, students, freebie seekers, unsupported geographies, or unrelated senses
rules.then: add exclusions to research, paid data, reporting, and content positioning
rules.else: retain the query in its valid cluster

rules.title: Build post-purchase search pathways
rules.if: customers search for setup, use, troubleshooting, maintenance, renewal, or complementary products
rules.then: create support and retention task clusters with appropriate next actions

rules.title: Start from parent concepts
rules.if: an offer lacks a mapped semantic territory
rules.then: identify parent concepts, neighboring categories, and business boundaries

rules.title: Expand through subtypes
rules.if: a parent concept contains meaningful narrower types with distinct tasks
rules.then: create subtype clusters and evaluate them independently
rules.else: keep subtype terms as sections or variants

rules.title: Normalize synonyms and paraphrases
rules.if: different phrases express the same sense and dominant task
rules.then: map them to one query cluster and one intended canonical asset

rules.title: Disambiguate homonyms and polysemy
rules.if: the same wording can refer to different concepts, entities, or tasks
rules.then: create sense labels and exclusions before clustering

rules.title: Model modifiers as facets
rules.if: terms vary by price, material, size, audience, platform, location, time, or other attributes
rules.then: represent them as attribute-value pairs and test whether they create a distinct task

rules.title: Use co-occurrence as context
rules.if: a term commonly appears near the topic but is not itself the user’s target
rules.then: use it only where it explains an entity, relation, attribute, or evidence need

rules.title: Map entities and relations
rules.if: the task depends on named things and how they connect
rules.then: record entity types and typed relations, then express those relations visibly

rules.title: Map query fan-out without page fan-out
rules.if: one broad task implies several supporting questions
rules.then: map the questions as sections, evidence needs, or distinct adjacent tasks
rules.else: do not create a separate page for every wording variation

rules.title: Triangulate demand evidence
rules.if: a candidate appears in only one tool or source
rules.then: seek corroboration from first-party data, users, result sets, competitors, or sales/support evidence
rules.else: increase confidence when independent sources agree

rules.title: Do not equate zero tool volume with zero demand
rules.if: a query has low or zero reported volume but appears in first-party or customer evidence
rules.then: retain it as a low-volume or emerging candidate and measure the cluster
rules.else: deprioritize only after value and evidence review

rules.title: Attach time state
rules.if: facts, prices, availability, standards, laws, events, or recommendations can change
rules.then: assign freshness requirements and update triggers
rules.else: classify the asset as stable evergreen

rules.title: Model emerging demand separately
rules.if: a new technology, regulation, event, or behavior has weak historical search data but strong causal evidence
rules.then: create an experimental demand thesis with explicit uncertainty

rules.title: One dominant intent, one owner
rules.if: a dominant intent cluster is approved
rules.then: assign exactly one intended canonical URL

rules.title: Merge same-task candidates
rules.if: sense, task, answer structure, result class, and next action are compatible
rules.then: merge candidates into one cluster

rules.title: Split different tasks
rules.if: queries share vocabulary but require different completion conditions or document forms
rules.then: create separate clusters and page roles

rules.title: Use result overlap as evidence, not law
rules.if: current top results overlap strongly for two queries
rules.then: increase merge confidence but still inspect task and business context
rules.else: do not force a split solely because result overlap is low

rules.title: Detect cannibalization by behavior
rules.if: multiple owned URLs receive the same cluster’s impressions with unstable dominance or divided value
rules.then: inspect intent, links, conversion, and canonical ownership
rules.else: allow multiple URLs when they serve genuinely different tasks
rules.primary_metric: dominant URL share and URL entropy

rules.title: Merge with migration discipline
rules.if: two pages are redundant and one combined page is superior
rules.then: merge best information, select the winner, redirect the loser, and update links/sitemaps

rules.title: Reposition a useful weaker page
rules.if: a weaker page has independent value but overlaps the stronger page’s task
rules.then: change its dominant intent and connect it as a supporting asset

rules.title: Inspect equity before deletion
rules.if: a page appears useless or redundant
rules.then: check links, traffic, conversions, references, and dependencies before delete/noindex

rules.title: Align canonical signals
rules.if: duplicate or parameter URLs must remain accessible
rules.then: align canonical annotations, internal links, sitemap entries, redirects, and content signals

rules.title: Protect established URLs
rules.if: an older URL has links, traffic, or history and the only proposed improvement is a prettier slug
rules.then: keep the URL unless expected benefit clearly exceeds migration risk
rules.else: optimize the new URL before launch

rules.title: Keep lexical variants together
rules.if: differences are spelling, word order, pluralization, abbreviation, or stemming without task change
rules.then: include natural variants in one asset and reporting cluster

rules.title: Test uncertain cluster boundaries
rules.if: merge/split evidence is inconclusive
rules.then: assign a provisional owner, record uncertainty, and observe query-to-URL behavior before scaling

rules.title: Select format from task
rules.if: the dominant task is known
rules.then: choose a format that completes that task: guide, table, calculator, map, diagnostic, template, video, or transaction page

rules.title: Answer early
rules.if: a user can benefit from a concise direct answer
rules.then: provide it near the beginning and then support it
rules.else: state the path to the answer and necessary prerequisites

rules.title: Require information advantage
rules.if: the proposed asset only restates widely available material
rules.then: add original experience, data, testing, utility, synthesis, local proof, or decision support

rules.title: Prefer firsthand evidence where relevant
rules.if: the task involves reviews, demonstrations, processes, products, or lived outcomes
rules.then: show what was actually tested, observed, used, or built
rules.else: use the best available primary evidence

rules.title: Make evidence visible
rules.if: a claim depends on a source, test, credential, or dataset
rules.then: place the supporting evidence where the user can inspect it
rules.else: qualify the claim as opinion or uncertainty

rules.title: State limitations
rules.if: evidence has uncertainty, sample limits, conflicts, exceptions, or changing conditions
rules.then: state limitations and applicability boundaries

rules.title: Avoid arbitrary length targets
rules.if: a word count is proposed without a task-based reason
rules.then: define completeness by required questions, evidence, and decision support
rules.else: use length as a production estimate only

rules.title: Govern AI-assisted content
rules.if: AI assists research, drafting, transformation, or scale
rules.then: require factual verification, original value, editorial ownership, and policy compliance
rules.else: use the same quality controls for human-only work

rules.title: Require row-level uniqueness at scale
rules.if: a template generates pages from a dataset
rules.then: require accurate unique data, distinct user utility, and a valid canonical task for each row
rules.else: consolidate rows into filters, tables, or broader assets

rules.title: Use media when it improves the task
rules.if: an image, diagram, video, audio, or interactive can explain or demonstrate more effectively
rules.then: include accessible, relevant media and measure its use
rules.else: keep the experience text-first where sufficient

rules.title: Define refresh triggers
rules.if: content depends on changing data or conditions
rules.then: assign owner, source, review cadence, and event-triggered updates
rules.else: review only when performance or business context changes

rules.title: Support commercial pages with useful assets
rules.if: a commercial page is important but difficult to cite or insufficient for research-stage users
rules.then: create genuinely useful supporting evidence, tools, comparisons, or guides

rules.title: Align the title with the task
rules.if: the title does not clearly identify the page’s dominant task or value
rules.then: rewrite it truthfully for relevance and useful differentiation

rules.title: Use unique titles for unique canonicals
rules.if: two intended indexable canonical pages use materially duplicate titles
rules.then: differentiate titles according to their distinct tasks
rules.else: allow shared patterns with unique identifying content

rules.title: Measure title changes causally
rules.if: a title or snippet is changed
rules.then: record change date, exposed queries/pages, expected mechanism, and CTR guardrails

rules.title: Write descriptions for decision support
rules.if: the result snippet can help users determine relevance
rules.then: write a concise truthful proposition with task, benefit, and distinguishing detail
rules.else: allow the search engine to select contextual text

rules.title: Use headings as answer architecture
rules.if: the task has stages, criteria, subquestions, or choices
rules.then: structure headings around those information functions

rules.title: Write natural body language
rules.if: required concepts, entities, attributes, and relations are missing
rules.then: add them where they improve the explanation
rules.else: do not insert terms solely for coverage scores

rules.title: Reject keyword stuffing
rules.if: repetition exists primarily to influence ranking rather than aid comprehension
rules.then: remove or rewrite it and preserve only natural references

rules.title: Describe meaningful images
rules.if: an image communicates information or functions as a link/control
rules.then: provide appropriate descriptive alternative text
rules.else: use empty alternative text for purely decorative images

rules.title: Optimize new URLs, protect old ones
rules.if: a page has not launched
rules.then: use a concise descriptive stable URL
rules.else: avoid changing an established URL without a migration case

rules.title: Use structured data only when applicable
rules.if: a supported structured-data type accurately represents visible page content
rules.then: implement and validate it
rules.else: do not add irrelevant or hidden markup

rules.title: Measure rich-result realization
rules.if: structured data validates successfully
rules.then: measure actual search appearance, impressions, CTR, and value
rules.else: debug eligibility or accept that display is not guaranteed

rules.title: Adjust CTR expectations
rules.if: CTR is evaluated
rules.then: control for position, device, country, brand status, query class, and search appearance
rules.else: do not use a universal CTR threshold

rules.title: Link every priority page
rules.if: a page is intended to receive organic visibility
rules.then: ensure at least one crawlable contextual internal link points to it
rules.else: remove it from the priority/index set if it has no valid role

rules.title: Use descriptive anchors
rules.if: anchor text is generic and a natural descriptive label is available
rules.then: replace it with concise context-setting text
rules.else: retain the generic control only when interface convention requires it

rules.title: Require user context for links
rules.if: a proposed link does not help the reader understand, compare, verify, or take the next step
rules.then: do not add it
rules.else: add it in the relevant sentence or interface

rules.title: Create hubs for navigation needs
rules.if: a coherent task family requires users to choose among multiple paths
rules.then: create or improve a hub with clear categories and routes
rules.else: connect assets contextually without a dedicated hub

rules.title: Validate supporting assets
rules.if: an adjacent question has independent demand, a complete answer, and a useful relationship to a core asset
rules.then: create a supporting asset and connect it
rules.else: include it as a section or FAQ

rules.title: Reduce excessive depth
rules.if: important pages are difficult to reach through internal navigation
rules.then: add meaningful paths, hubs, or template links
rules.else: retain depth for low-value or intentionally isolated pages

rules.title: Use strong internal sources deliberately
rules.if: an authoritative owned page can naturally support a high-value target
rules.then: add a contextual link where it benefits the reader
rules.else: do not insert an unrelated link solely to move authority

rules.title: Keep topical communities coherent
rules.if: a link crosses unrelated topic communities without user need
rules.then: remove or avoid it
rules.else: retain cross-topic links that represent a real prerequisite, comparison, or journey edge

rules.title: Make links crawlable
rules.if: navigation or internal discovery relies on nonstandard scripted interactions
rules.then: expose crawlable anchors with destinations and validate rendered HTML

rules.title: Concentrate, do not hoard
rules.if: many low-value pages dilute attention and internal graph flow
rules.then: consolidate, noindex, archive, or demote according to user and business value

rules.title: Update the graph after migrations
rules.if: a page is merged, redirected, renamed, or retired
rules.then: update internal links, navigation, canonicals, and sitemaps to the final destination

rules.title: Measure paths, not link counts alone
rules.if: internal linking is evaluated
rules.then: measure discovery, depth, target visibility, task progression, and conversion paths
rules.else: use raw link counts only as diagnostics

rules.title: Evaluate link quality multidimensionally
rules.if: an external link opportunity is considered
rules.then: evaluate relevance, editorial independence, source credibility, placement, uniqueness, and persistence

rules.title: Create a linkable reason
rules.if: outreach asks for attention without a concrete user benefit
rules.then: build or identify data, utility, evidence, correction, visualization, or unique reference value

rules.title: Support difficult commercial targets
rules.if: the target commercial page is unlikely to earn independent citations
rules.then: earn links to a relevant useful asset and connect it to the target OR improve the target’s reference value

rules.title: Reject manipulative placements
rules.if: a link requires deception, irrelevant insertion, undisclosed payment, or policy violation
rules.then: reject it
rules.else: proceed with transparent editorial or appropriately attributed placement

rules.title: Prefer unique relevant domains
rules.if: many links come repeatedly from the same source while relevant independent sources are available
rules.then: diversify outreach toward unique relevant domains
rules.else: deepen the useful relationship without treating every link as independent authority

rules.title: Prefer contextual editorial placement
rules.if: a link can appear in a useful body context or only in a repeated footer/sidebar
rules.then: prefer the contextual editorial placement
rules.else: treat repeated placement as lower-confidence evidence

rules.title: Use tool metrics as proxies
rules.if: DA, DR, UR, PA, traffic estimates, or difficulty scores are used
rules.then: treat them as vendor-specific diagnostics and compare within one system

rules.title: Investigate lost evidence
rules.if: a valuable relevant link or mention disappears
rules.then: classify cause and recover only when the source relationship and user value remain valid

rules.title: Measure brand demand effects
rules.if: earned media or authoritative mentions may increase awareness without direct referral clicks
rules.then: track branded queries, direct visits, assisted conversions, and target visibility
rules.else: measure direct referral and link effects

rules.title: Segment outreach by relationship
rules.if: prospects differ by audience, reason to care, or editorial context
rules.then: create distinct outreach propositions and evidence packages
rules.primary_metric: positive reply and placement rate by segment

rules.title: Compound original research
rules.if: original data or a benchmark performs well
rules.then: refresh it, expose methodology, create reusable views, and connect related clusters
rules.else: treat it as a one-time asset

rules.title: Judge authority by target outcomes
rules.if: links or mentions increase but the target cluster does not improve
rules.then: inspect relevance, target selection, indexing, content fit, and time lag
rules.else: continue scaling the validated authority mechanism

rules.title: Require public accessibility
rules.if: a page is intended for search visibility
rules.then: ensure users and permitted crawlers can request its essential content

rules.title: Use correct response states
rules.if: a canonical page is healthy and available
rules.then: return a successful response; use redirects, not-found, or server errors only for their true states

rules.title: Validate rendered main content
rules.if: essential content or links depend on JavaScript
rules.then: inspect rendered output and ensure resources are accessible

rules.title: Separate crawling from indexing controls
rules.if: the goal is to keep a page out of search results
rules.then: use an appropriate noindex, authentication, removal, redirect, or deletion method
rules.else: use robots.txt only to manage crawler requests, not as a deindex guarantee

rules.title: Maintain canonical coherence
rules.if: multiple URLs represent substantially the same content
rules.then: select a preferred URL and align canonical, redirects where appropriate, links, and sitemap signals
rules.else: self-canonicalize the unique asset where useful

rules.title: Keep sitemaps canonical and current
rules.if: a URL is important, canonical, and intended for indexing
rules.then: include its clean URL and accurate modification state in the sitemap
rules.else: exclude noncanonical, redirected, error, or intentionally nonindexed URLs

rules.title: Redirect to the closest valid successor
rules.if: a URL permanently moves or is consolidated
rules.then: redirect directly to the most relevant final destination and update internal references

rules.title: Treat not-found pages intentionally
rules.if: a resource no longer exists and has no valid replacement
rules.then: return a real not-found state with helpful navigation
rules.else: redirect only when a genuine equivalent exists

rules.title: Control faceted and parameter volume
rules.if: filters, sorting, search, tracking, or session parameters create many near-duplicate URLs
rules.then: define crawl, canonical, link, and index rules by facet value

rules.title: Preserve content parity
rules.if: mobile, desktop, locale, or rendered versions differ
rules.then: ensure essential content, metadata, structured data, and links remain equivalent where they should

rules.title: Prioritize real-user performance
rules.if: field performance or business outcomes show latency, instability, or interaction problems
rules.then: fix the highest-exposure causes and measure Core Web Vitals plus conversion/task outcomes
rules.else: repair only obvious low-cost issues and avoid score chasing

rules.title: Scale crawl work to site size and change rate
rules.if: the site is very large, rapidly changing, or shows crawl/index waste
rules.then: invest in crawl-path, logs, facets, and index-quality optimization
rules.else: use a lighter periodic technical audit
rules.primary_metric: valuable indexed URLs per crawl/resource unit

rules.title: Complete the search task before selling
rules.if: the page asks for conversion before delivering the promised answer
rules.then: front-load useful task completion and place the offer at a logical transition

rules.title: Match nudge to journey state
rules.if: the next action is not adjacent to the user’s current state
rules.then: choose a lower-friction or more relevant action

rules.title: Optimize speed for outcomes
rules.if: slow or unstable experience correlates with abandonment or conversion loss
rules.then: fix the responsible bottleneck and validate field/user outcomes
rules.else: do not pursue a perfect tool score solely for ranking
rules.primary_metric: conversion and task completion by performance band

rules.title: Reduce form friction selectively
rules.if: form abandonment is high AND removed fields are not needed for qualification or routing
rules.then: shorten, stage, or clarify the form

rules.title: Optimize for lead quality
rules.if: lead count rises while acceptance, close rate, or margin falls
rules.then: tighten intent, promise, qualification, or routing

rules.title: Test CTA propositions, not colors alone
rules.if: a CTA underperforms
rules.then: test task relevance, value, risk, evidence, commitment, placement, and wording before cosmetic variables

rules.title: Place trust at the decision point
rules.if: users hesitate because scope, proof, identity, terms, price, or risk is unclear
rules.then: place relevant evidence and clarification near the decision

rules.title: Avoid premature hard selling
rules.if: the query is early-stage and commercial pressure harms task satisfaction
rules.then: use a useful soft transition such as a related guide, tool, save, or diagnostic

rules.title: Design retention paths
rules.if: the organic visitor is an existing customer or user
rules.then: route to successful use, support, renewal, expansion, or advocacy

rules.title: Measure satisfaction with task-specific events
rules.if: generic engagement metrics cannot show whether the task was completed
rules.then: instrument meaningful events such as calculator completion, comparison use, download, copy, or successful route

rules.title: Preserve message continuity
rules.if: the search promise, landing answer, CTA, and sales follow-up describe different outcomes
rules.then: align the chain around one user task and offer

rules.title: Protect user and brand guardrails
rules.if: a conversion intervention increases action but also complaints, refunds, low-quality leads, or distrust
rules.then: revert, constrain, or redesign the intervention
rules.else: continue while guardrails stay within tolerance

rules.title: Require a mechanism hypothesis
rules.if: an intervention has no stated reason it should affect an outcome
rules.then: write an object → action → mechanism → outcome hypothesis

rules.title: Capture a baseline
rules.if: a change is about to be implemented
rules.then: record pre-change performance, context, exposure, and data quality

rules.title: Use a change ledger
rules.if: any SEO-relevant production change occurs
rules.then: assign a change ID, owner, scope, time, expected mechanism, and rollback state

rules.title: Choose one primary metric
rules.if: an experiment has many possible success metrics
rules.then: select one primary decision metric and label others secondary or guardrail

rules.title: Set guardrails before launch
rules.if: a change can improve the primary metric while harming quality, accessibility, revenue, or trust
rules.then: define guardrail thresholds and rollback behavior

rules.title: Use controls when feasible
rules.if: comparable untreated pages, clusters, regions, or time periods exist
rules.then: use a control or difference-in-differences design
rules.else: use interrupted time series with explicit limitations

rules.title: Account for seasonality and external events
rules.if: demand, algorithms, campaigns, news, inventory, or holidays can affect the outcome
rules.then: annotate and model those factors before attributing change

rules.title: Represent uncertainty
rules.if: sample size is small, variance is high, or exposure is incomplete
rules.then: report ranges, confidence, and directional evidence

rules.title: Allow processing and learning time
rules.if: a change has not had enough crawl, index, ranking, or behavioral exposure
rules.then: continue observation until the predefined minimum exposure or stop condition

rules.title: Distinguish single-variable and package tests
rules.if: several material variables change together
rules.then: classify the intervention as a package test OR separate variables for causal learning
rules.else: treat it as a focused test

rules.title: Escalate by diagnosed mechanism
rules.if: a lower-level LAKA intervention fails
rules.then: re-diagnose and move to Major, Structural, or Paradigm only when the failure mechanism requires it
rules.else: retain or scale the successful level

rules.title: Use explicit continue/revise/revert/retire decisions
rules.if: a review point is reached
rules.then: choose exactly one decision based on primary metric, guardrails, cost, and confidence
rules.else: continue observation only under a predefined uncertainty rule

rules.title: Keep foundational SEO as the base
rules.if: the goal includes visibility in generative search experiences
rules.then: apply the same valuable-content, crawlability, indexability, and search-quality foundations

rules.title: Do not depend on llms.txt for Google Search
rules.if: a proposal claims a special AI text file is required for Google visibility
rules.then: reject the requirement and prioritize public crawlable indexable content
rules.else: maintain such a file only for a separate system that explicitly uses it

rules.title: Do not chunk content mechanically
rules.if: content is being split only because an AI system is assumed to need tiny sections
rules.then: organize by human task, readability, and information structure

rules.title: Use query fan-out as a research map
rules.if: a broad request implies related information needs
rules.then: map prerequisite, comparison, evidence, and follow-up needs across the cluster graph

rules.title: Block scaled content abuse
rules.if: content volume is generated primarily to manipulate rankings or AI responses without distinct user value
rules.then: stop publication and redesign the system
rules.else: continue only with row-level utility, accuracy, and governance

rules.title: Measure generative visibility directly
rules.if: Search Console or another first-party surface provides generative-search reporting
rules.then: track it as a distinct search appearance and connect it to downstream value
rules.else: use broader search and referral diagnostics with limitations

rules.title: Do not invent AI-specific schema
rules.if: a proposal adds unsupported structured data solely for generative visibility
rules.then: reject it; use supported structured data only when it matches visible content

rules.title: Prepare for agentic use through usability
rules.if: browser agents or assistive systems need to interpret and operate the site
rules.then: improve semantic controls, labels, accessible structure, clear states, and stable data
rules.primary_metric: successful task completion by automated/assistive clients

rules.title: Expose freshness and provenance
rules.if: data may change or be reused in generated answers
rules.then: show dates, methodology, sources, ownership, and update state where useful

rules.title: Constrain programmatic expansion
rules.if: candidate combinations exceed quality or maintenance capacity
rules.then: raise gates, consolidate, stage release, or automate verified data maintenance

rules.title: Protect privacy, consent, and sensitive data
rules.if: volumetric generation or personalization uses personal, confidential, licensed, or restricted data
rules.then: minimize data, obtain rights/consent, secure access, and exclude unsafe outputs
rules.else: use public or owned permissible data

rules.title: Pursue paradigm assets selectively
rules.if: a new tool, dataset, benchmark, diagnostic, or agent can complete the task far better than existing result classes
rules.then: run a bounded paradigm experiment with a defensibility and maintenance plan
